title: Italian Antipasto Board
seo_title: Italian Antipasto Board for 8–12: Shopping List & Plan
description: An Italian antipasto board for 8–12: Parmigiano, mozzarella, provolone, prosciutto, mortadella, artichokes, olives and focaccia. What to buy and a 60-minute plan.
hook: The board that tastes like the start of a long Italian lunch: salty, briny, a little sweet, and built almost entirely from the deli counter and a few jars.
why: Antipasto works on contrast. Rich, fatty meats like mortadella and coppa sit next to sharp, tangy things from jars: pepperoncini, artichokes and roasted peppers. Every bite of meat gets reset by something bright.

The three cheeses cover three textures: crumbly, salty Parmigiano, soft and milky mozzarella, and firm, sharp provolone. Balsamic glaze over the Parmigiano and honey beside the provolone add the sweet notes, so the board doesn't need jam.

timeline.what: Take the Parmigiano out of the fridge.
Take out the provolone; drain the olives, artichokes and peppers.
Take out the meats and mozzarella; slice the focaccia.
Break the Parmigiano into chunks; place the cheeses and fold the meats.
Fill the gaps with olives and almonds; drizzle oil and balsamic; add basil.

faq.q: What's the difference between antipasto and charcuterie?
faq.a: Charcuterie is mostly cured meat and cheese. Antipasto, the Italian starter course, adds marinated and pickled vegetables, olives and bread, so it's lighter and brighter.

faq.q: How many people does this antipasto board serve?
faq.a: 8 to 12 people on a 20–26 inch board. As the main party food, plan about 3 oz each of meat and cheese per guest.
Drain the jarred vegetables and cut the hard cheeses up to a day ahead and keep them covered in the fridge. Assemble within an hour of serving and leave it out no more than 2 hours.
